pdfImport.title: Import Preview
pdfImport.help: Check how each line of the PDF was read. Select lines — shift-click for a range, ⌘/Ctrl-click or tick to add one — then set their type. Nothing changes in the open script until you press Import.
pdfImport.sameTypeTitle: Select every line of the type(s) already selected
pdfImport.sameIndentTitle: Select every line at the same indent, in the same case, as those already selected
pdfImport.rangeTitle: Select everything from the last line you picked to the next line you tap

pdfSecurity.title: PDF with Watermark or Password
pdfSecurity.pageFoot: At the foot of the page
pdfSecurity.recipientsHelp: One name per line. Each copy is watermarked with its name — put {recipient} in the text to place it — and all of them are saved together in a .zip.
pdfSecurity.restrictionsHelp: PDF restrictions keep honest readers honest; they use the PDF standard’s basic encryption, which determined software can remove. The watermark is what identifies a leaked copy.

sceneSpacing.title: Use standard scene heading spacing?
sceneSpacing.intro: This script puts one blank line before each scene heading. Industry standard — and Final Draft’s default — is two.
sceneSpacing.explanation: Reformatting changes where pages break, so the script will get slightly longer. You can change it at any time under Format › Formatting Template, and this script keeps whichever you choose.
